english_description: A proleptic Gregorian date with validity, day-count conversion, and a bounded round-trip query.

queries.english: Whether the year, month, and day form a valid Gregorian date.
The epoch day count produced by the total civil-date conversion.
The day count produced within the supported date-subset range.
Whether converting this valid date to days and back preserves every field.

constraints.english: to_days returns the proleptic Gregorian day-count formula for the stored year, month, and day without requiring ok().
from_days returns the Gregorian year, month, and day recovered from its input epoch-day count.
constraints.logic: result.year.0@ == civil_from_days(dp.0@).year && result.month.0@ == civil_from_days(dp.0@).month && result.day.0@ == civil_from_days(dp.0@).day

constraints.english: ok() is true exactly when the year and month are valid and the day is between one and that month's Gregorian length.
constraints.logic: result == (self.year.0@ != -32768 && 1 <= self.month.0@ && self.month.0@ <= 12 && 1 <= self.day.0@ && self.day.0@ <= month_length(self.month.0@, self.year.0@))

constraints.english: For supported year inputs, to_days_bounded stays within the signed 32-bit day-count interval.
For a valid supported date, round_trip returns true exactly when converting the date to an epoch-day count and back preserves its year, month, and day.
constraints.logic: result == (civil_from_days(days_from_civil(self.year.0@, self.month.0@, self.day.0@)).year == self.year.0@ && civil_from_days(days_from_civil(self.year.0@, self.month.0@, self.day.0@)).month == self.month.0@ && civil_from_days(days_from_civil(self.year.0@, self.month.0@, self.day.0@)).day == self.day.0@)

adversary_table.scenario: A bounded epoch-day input is decoded into a different civil year, month, or day.
adversary_table.resolution: Return the exact year, month, and day computed by civil_from_days for that input.

adversary_table.scenario: February 30 is rejected before the total to_days conversion runs.
adversary_table.resolution: Keep conversion total and compute the reference civil day-count formula.

adversary_table.scenario: The largest supported year produces a day count outside the 32-bit interval.
adversary_table.resolution: Return a representable day count within the declared bounds.

adversary_table.scenario: A valid leap-day date converts to an epoch day and returns with one field changed.
adversary_table.resolution: Return true only when the recovered year, month, and day equal the original fields.

source_references.notes: Pinned year_month_day data model, ok(), sys_days conversion, and to_days/from_days declarations; supported by accepted E-1, E-2, E-4, E-12, and E-15.
Accepted E-9 supplies direct round-trip and leap-century cases; accepted E-14 records bounded domain endpoints.
Creusot ensures for from_days (C002) and round_trip (C007); these declarations specify intended scope and do not assert that a fresh proof has passed.
